title: Closed-immersion transport of a power-annihilated formal kernel
statement: Let j:Z -> X be a closed immersion of Noetherian schemes [def-weil-closed-immersion], f:X -> S with j followed by f locally of finite type, and Q a quasi-coherent ideal. Choose any Abelian structure on Coh(X,Q) [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-modules-abelian]. Let M in Coh(X,Q) and G in Coh(Z,Q O_Z) [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module] be identified by M ~= j_*G as inverse systems. Let H be a coherent module on Z with support proper over S [pqf-def-coherent, def-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base]. Let L be a quasi-coherent ideal with nonempty complement of V(L). Given alpha:G -> H^wedge, a positive integer t and a limiting kernel fork k for alpha whose point is annihilated termwise by L^t, there exist N in Coh(X,Q), a:M -> N, and an ideal J strictly containing j.ker, such that J annihilates kernel a. Moreover some closed subscheme T -> X proper over S annihilates N.

source.place: Theorem 088E, paragraphs 2--4 (closed quotient, Chow modification, projective algebraization and proper push-pull comparison); verified at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/088E

proof.text: Use the closed formal pushforward equivalence and its comparison with completion to push alpha to X. Compose on its source with the specified inverse-system isomorphism M ~= j_*G. Fullness of the formal inclusion produces the actual coherent formal morphism a:M -> N, where N is the pushed completion of H.

Let B=L^t and define J by inverse image under O_X -> j_*O_Z. On affine opens these are inverse images of ideals under quotient ring maps, and they agree upon localization, hence define a quasi-coherent ideal. Its kernel is j.ker, so j.ker <= J. At a point of the nonempty open Z minus V(L), L^t has unit stalk; B is therefore nonzero, which makes this containment strict.

The limiting fork identifies k.pt with the kernel of alpha. Closed pushforward is exact and the formal full subcategory of objects killed by j.ker is closed under kernels in the ambient formal category. Thus the pushforward of k.pt, after the source comparison, is the ambient kernel of a. On affine opens the J action on a pushed module factors through the B action. The hypothesis that B kills all terms of k.pt therefore kills all terms of kernel a.

Apply the scheme-theoretic support characterization to coherent H. It gives a closed subscheme i:T -> Z whose ideal annihilates H and which is proper over S. Its ideal also annihilates every adic quotient of H. The composite i followed by j is closed and remains proper over S. The quotient-ring action calculation shows that its kernel annihilates each term of the pushed completion N.

theorem exists_closedImmersionFormalComparisonTransport
    {X Z S : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian X] [IsNoetherian Z]
    (f : X ⟶ S) (j : Z ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion j]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (j ≫ f)] (Q : X.IdealSheafData)
    [Abelian (CoherentFormalModule X Q)]
    (M : CoherentFormalModule X Q) (G : CoherentFormalModule Z (Q.comap j))
    (e : M.obj ≅ G.obj ⋙ Scheme.Modules.pushforward j)
    (H : CoherentModules Z)
    (hH : Scheme.Modules.HasSupportProperOver (j ≫ f) H.obj)
    (L : Z.IdealSheafData) (hU : (L.support.compl : Set Z).Nonempty)
    (α : G ⟶ (completion Z (Q.comap j)).obj H)
    (t : ℕ) (ht : 1 ≤ t) (k : KernelFork α) (hk : IsLimit k)
    (hkill : ∀ n : ℕ, IsZero (Scheme.idealModuleProduct
      (Scheme.idealSheafPower L.toModulesι t).2 (k.pt.obj.obj (op n)))) :
    ∃ (N : CoherentFormalModule X Q) (a : M ⟶ N) (J : X.IdealSheafData),
      j.ker < J ∧ AnnihilatedBy Q J (kernel a) ∧
      ∃ (T : Scheme.{u}) (i : T ⟶ X) (_ : IsClosedImmersion i),
        IsProper (i ≫ f) ∧ AnnihilatedBy Q i.ker N
